result.summary:
Venkataraman et al. 2022 ran BS-Snper nine times: once on a samtools-merged BAM of the 8 animals and once on each animal's BAM, with defaults except --mincover 5. They kept every VCF record that overlaps a CG motif and matches grep "C<TAB>T" (REF C with ALT T, or ALT "T,G"), whatever its FILTER (PASS or Low), QUAL or depth, and took the union. They then removed CpGs at those positions in two places: from the 5x CpG sets of the global characterisation (subtractBed) and from the DML list after the test (intersectBed -u / subtractBed). The methylKit input, the united table, the model fits and the q-values were not changed.

I reproduced their numbers from their own tables on gannet:
- The 300,278 "C->T SNPs" are 300,032 distinct positions. 246 positions appear twice, once with ALT T and once with ALT T,G.
- Every one of the 300,032 is the C of a CpG on the plus strand (checked against the genome). G>A at the CpG's G, which is the same change on the minus strand, was not excluded.
- 48,405 positions (16.1%) rest only on FILTER=Low records. 48,466 never had 5 or more opposite-strand reads in any of the nine runs, and 21,119 never had more than one opposite-strand T read. So the 5x setting only changed the PASS/Low label and had no effect on what was excluded.
- 315 of their 1,599 DML have their C in the list, which matches the article. The count falls to 266 if only PASS records are used and to 192 if only the merged-file run is used.
- The article's 11,238,223 CpGs is a line count that includes the header line; the file holds 11,238,222 CpGs.

BS-Snper rule (read from source):
- Reads with MAPQ under 20 and unmapped reads are dropped. Bases with quality under 15 become N.
- A read is dropped if it has more than round(0.02 x length) mismatches that bisulfite conversion cannot explain.
- Reads are split into Watson (FLAG 99/147) and Crick (FLAG 83/163). Bismark 0.22.3 swaps the flags of the CTOT and CTOB strands, so this directional assumption groups the non-directional reads correctly.
- At a reference C, Watson T is counted as C. The C>T candidate rate is Crick T / (Crick C + Crick T), and the site is a candidate if this is above 0.1.
- A diploid Bayes model with priors (cc 0.985, ct 0.000667, tt 0.00033) picks the genotype. A CT call then needs at least 3 Crick T reads.
- Every non-reference genotype is written to the VCF as PASS or Low.
- --maxcover is never used. Only the last CIGAR operation of each read is kept (a bug, confirmed with a compiled test: "66M7I7M" becomes "7M").

spec.md gives an R specification (Rsamtools/GenomicAlignments). The "merged" call can be done by summing per-library counts; this is exact because every filter acts on single reads.

Triploids: a single variant copy (expected T share 1/3) and a double copy (2/3) are both above the 0.1 threshold and below the 0.85 homozygous threshold, so both are labelled heterozygous. Detection is lower for a single copy. At 5 opposite-strand reads the call probability is 0.21 for 1/3, 0.50 for a diploid heterozygote and 0.79 for 2/3; at 10 reads it is 0.70, 0.95 and 1.00. Pooled over 22 libraries, a call needs about 15% T among the pooled opposite-strand reads. That is about 7 of 22 diploid heterozygous carriers, or about 11 single-copy triploids.

result.recommendation:
Build the toggle so that its default setting reproduces the 2022 rule exactly:
- **Which calls:** the union of a pooled call (per-library counts summed over the 22 libraries, which equals a merged BAM) and 22 per-library calls.
- **Which records:** any record with REF C and ALT T or T,G at the C of a CpG, whatever its FILTER.
- **Where:** remove those CpGs from the global-characterisation CpG sets and from the DML lists after the test, leaving fits and q-values unchanged.

Port BS-Snper's read filters, counting, candidate rule, Bayes genotype and post-rules exactly, as written in spec.md. Use scanBam rather than Rsamtools::pileup defaults (pileup caps depth at 250, has its own base-quality default and drops flags silently). Offer two separately labelled settings, each off: PASS only, and checking the G of each CpG as well. Before using the port, check it against real BS-Snper output, once with BS-Snper's last-CIGAR-operation behaviour switched on. Do this on one small sequence of the 2022 study's BAMs, fetched from gannet by range requests, against their CT-SNPs tables.
open_points: Plus-strand C only (exactly as in 2022) or both C and G of each CpG. The coverage files merge both strands, so the 2022 rule keeps CpGs whose minus-strand C carries the variant. This is the author's decision.
Any FILTER (as in 2022; 16.1% of their excluded positions rest on Low records only) or PASS only. This is the author's decision; the default should reproduce 2022.
Pooled call over all 22 libraries (as in 2022, where the 8 animals came from one experiment) or one pool per experiment. This project has two experiments sequenced separately (I-01).
Whether the 22 BAM files of this project are still on gannet under /panopea/061021-big/ was not checked. The R implementation needs them, with their indexes.
The master branch of BS-Snper was assumed to equal the April 2021 download, because the commit history could not be read. A validation run against the 2022 study's outputs would settle this.
I did not read the supplementary text of Gao et al. 2015 (Table S1 with the rate formulae); the source code was used instead.
How many reads in these BAMs have indels, and so how much BS-Snper's CIGAR bug matters, is unmeasured without the BAMs.
Rsamtools::pileup's min_base_quality scale (Phred or ASCII) was not tested. The spec avoids pileup for that reason.

My scratch directory already held files from an earlier attempt at this step, dated 00:32 to 00:44, before my first command at 00:46: code/bssnper_rule_check.py, ct_union_stats.py, dml_snp_overlap.py, nbdump.py, osf_ls.py and downloads/gannet_2022, osf_code, osf_dml, PMC9351233.*. I did not use them, and spec.md is mine.
risks: Without a validation run against the 2022 study's BS-Snper output, an R port can carry an undetected difference. The Bayes step and the post-rules are easy to get subtly wrong.

Exclusion sensitivity depends on ploidy. At 5 opposite-strand reads a single-copy triploid allele is detected with probability 0.21, against 0.50 for a diploid heterozygote. Masking can therefore treat the two groups of a ploidy contrast unequally.

At this project's depth (6 to 12 reads per position over the genome), per-library detection is low. Many variant CpGs will stay unmasked, while the any-FILTER rule also masks sites on a single opposite-strand T read.
Reading 22 BAMs of about 10 GB each in R is heavy in time and I/O. It needs per-chromosome chunking with yieldSize and must respect the memory limits of the other workflow.
Rsamtools::pileup defaults (max_depth 250, min_base_quality 13, silent exclusion of some flags) would silently change the calls if used.

result.summary:
All 22 sorted, deduplicated Bismark alignments of the June to July 2021 run are on gannet, each with its index. Together they hold 109,107,652,888 bytes (109.1 GB). The smallest is 3.35 GB (zr3644_14) and the largest 6.76 GB (zr3534_8). The 22 indexes hold 34.2 MB.

No variant calls exist for these libraries. I sent 96 HEAD requests for the BS-Snper output names, built on the OSF notebook of Venkataraman et al. 2022, to /panopea/061021-big/ and to the project directory and its data/ and analyses/ folders. All came back 404. The project manifest has no line matching snp, vcf or bam.

R can read regions of the remote BAMs directly. Rhtslib 2.4.1 and Rsamtools 2.18.0 link libcurl, and the proxy variables are already set. With a local copy of the .bai, a two-base query that opens a new BamFile per call runs at 38.7 queries per minute (200 queries in 309.9 s). Putting 200 ranges into one scanBam call is slower, at 14.4 per minute. A BamFile that is opened once and reused returns reads only for the first query and silently returns 0 for every later one. About 2.5% of opens fail with "Software caused connection abort" and need a retry.

Download speed from gannet varies between 2.0 and 21.5 MB/s per stream; two 300 MB ranges ran at 2.78 and 8.43 MB/s. Downloading all 22 BAMs would take about 3.6 to 10.9 hours, or 20 to 40 minutes per BAM at the slow rate. About 31 GB of disk is free, so one BAM at a time (at most 6.8 GB), deleted after use, fits.

I profiled 3,656 alignments of the heat library zr3534_1 and 2,615 of the control zr3644_1. Only four FLAG values occur: 99, 147, 83 and 163. Every one is paired and proper; none is unmapped, secondary, duplicate, supplementary or QC-failed. The tags XR, XG, XM, NM and MD are on 100% of reads. The XR/XG pair is fixed by the FLAG: 99 is CT/CT, 147 is GA/CT, 83 is CT/GA and 163 is GA/GA. Both mates of a pair always carry the same XG (1,821 of 1,821 pairs and 1,300 of 1,300). The FLAG pairs 99/147 and 83/163 therefore give the DNA strand of origin, which is the rule BS-Snper uses.

The original top strand and its complement (OT and CTOT) cannot be told apart in these BAMs, and neither can OB and CTOB. Bismark 0.22.3 swaps the R1 and R2 FLAGs for CTOT and CTOB pairs. Only the genomic strand is needed for the variant rule, so this does not matter.

Mates overlap in 85% (heat) and 89% (control) of pairs, with a median overlap of 77 to 78 bp. Rsamtools::pileup counts both mates where they overlap; at one position it gave a depth of 13 from 8 fragments. Bismark's methylation extractor counts each fragment once, because --no_overlap is its default for paired-end data. Counts that match the coverage files therefore need counting per fragment, not pileup.

facts.claim: Item 3: R reads regions of the remote BAM without downloading the file. Rhtslib 2.4.1 (libhts.so and Rhtslib.so) and Rsamtools 2.18.0 (Rsamtools.so) link libcurl.so.4, and https_proxy and CURL_CA_BUNDLE=/root/.ccr/ca-bundle.crt are already set in the environment. scanBamHeader on the URL took 2.1 s and returned 237 sequences (647,905,321 bp), SO:coordinate, and the @PG line of Bismark v0.22.3 with --non_directional -score_min L,0,-0.6. The timing run used 200 two-base regions, placed at random across the genome in proportion to sequence length (seed 20261120), on zr3534_1 with a local .bai. With a new BamFile per call it took 309.9 s, which is 38.7 queries per minute. The median query took 1.28 s, the 90th percentile 1.61 s and the slowest 10.26 s. 5 of the 200 opens failed with 'Software caused connection abort'. The other 195 regions gave 11.6 reads on average (median 8; 48 regions had none). A single scanBam call with all 200 ranges took 833.8 s (14.4 per minute); for the first 20 regions its counts were identical to those of the per-call method. A BamFile opened once with open() and reused is not usable remotely. On 20 regions it returned reads only for the first query and 0 for the other 19 without any error, where new handles found reads in 9 of them. The R process stayed at about 380 MB of memory. I did not try fetching byte ranges myself, because htslib works. The pieces for it exist in R (the curl and httr packages, readBin for the .bai, memDecompress for BGZF blocks), but it would mean writing a BAM record parser in R, which is not practical when Rsamtools does it.

facts.claim: Item 5: I profiled alignments from three 10 kb windows (NC_047561.1:20,000,001 to 20,010,000; NC_047564.1:30,000,001 to 30,010,000; NC_047567.1:15,000,001 to 15,010,000), each read in about 3 s. Heat library zr3534_1: 3,656 alignments from 1,835 read names. FLAG 99 (849), 147 (848), 83 (977), 163 (982), with no other values. All are paired and proper pairs; none is unmapped, mate-unmapped, secondary, QC-failed, duplicate or supplementary. MAPQ: 197 at 0, 638 at 2 to 9, 76 at 10 to 19, 659 at 20 to 29, 56 at 30 to 39, 2,030 at 40 to 42; median 40; 75.1% at 20 or above. Read lengths run from 16 to 115 (median 115; 2,083 at 115). There is no soft clipping, and 31% of reads have an insertion or deletion. XR, XG, XM, NM and MD are present on 100% of reads. XR/XG by FLAG: 99 is CT/CT, 147 is GA/CT, 83 is CT/GA, 163 is GA/GA, with no exceptions. Both mates share XG in 1,821 of 1,821 complete pairs. The mates overlap in 84.8% of pairs (median overlap 77 bp, mean 72). The median |TLEN| of the first-flagged mate is 133. No mate maps to another sequence. Control library zr3644_1: 2,615 alignments from 1,315 names. FLAG 99 (596), 147 (593), 83 (714), 163 (712). All proper pairs. MAPQ 185 at 0, median 40, 75.5% at 20 or above. Same tags, and the same XR/XG to FLAG mapping. Both mates share XG in 1,300 of 1,300 pairs. The mates overlap in 88.9% of pairs (median 78 bp). The Bismark 0.22.3 source sets the FLAGs as OT R1/R2 99/147, OB 83/163, CTOT 147/99 and CTOB 163/83. The R1 and R2 flags are swapped for CTOT and CTOB 'so that we don't end up with discordant pairs'. OT and CTOT are therefore indistinguishable in these BAMs, and so are OB and CTOB. The genomic strand of origin is given exactly by the FLAG pair: 99/147 (XG CT) is the top strand, 83/163 (XG GA) the bottom strand. The June PE report of zr3534_1 confirms that all four strands are present (OT 11,745,478; CTOT 11,768,014; CTOB 11,776,680; OB 11,756,670).

facts.claim: Item 6: An R script that counts bases by strand of origin at a list of CpGs needs the following. (a) Strand of origin by FLAG, as BS-Snper does. In sam_funcs.c, parseBuffer sets the strand from 0x10 and the read number from 0x80. snpProcess counts Watson for (+, read 1) and (-, read 2), which are FLAGs 99 and 147, and Crick for 83 and 163. In these BAMs that is identical to XG. scanBamFlag cannot express OR, so each strand takes two flag-filtered queries: top is isFirstMateRead=TRUE with isMinusStrand=FALSE, plus isSecondMateRead=TRUE with isMinusStrand=TRUE; bottom is the other two combinations. I checked this: four pileup() calls on 400 bp of a remote BAM took 5.1 s and returned the expected strands. Filtering on the XG tag (scanBam tag='XG', or a FilterRules function in filterBam) gives the same split but is not needed. (b) Counting each fragment once. pileup() counts both overlapping mates. At 7 positions its depth equalled the number of alignments, which exceeded the number of distinct fragments (for example 13 against 8, and 28 against 18). Bismark's methylation extractor sets --no_overlap by default for paired-end data, so the coverage files count fragments. To match them, use scanBam (qname, flag, pos, cigar, seq, qual; tag XG), take the base at each target position (for example with GenomicAlignments::pileLettersAt or sequenceLayer), then remove duplicates by qname within each strand. BS-Snper itself has no mate-overlap logic as far as I can see: grep for mate, overlap and isize in sam_funcs.c found nothing. (c) The rule's inputs. For a C on the top strand, the evidence is the bottom-strand reads (FLAG 83/163), with G for the reference allele and A for a C-to-T variant. For the G of the CpG, the evidence is the top-strand reads (99/147), with G against A. On the converted strand itself, BS-Snper counts a T at a reference C as C (Watson, read 1) and an A at a reference G as G (Crick, read 2 on +). Thresholds to carry over: base quality 15, MAPQ 20 (75% of the reads sampled here pass), minimum depth 5. result.recommendation:
How the variant toggle (off by default) should get its data depends on how many CpGs it covers.

- **Candidate DML only:** remote region queries in R are enough. Use Rsamtools with a local .bai, a new BamFile for every query, and a retry when an open fails. Never reuse an opened remote BamFile: after the first query it returns 0 reads without any error. The DML lists number about 3,189 distinct CpGs (1,038 + 2,351 - 200, from issues.md I-02). At the measured 38.7 queries per minute that is about 82 minutes per library, or about 30 hours for all 22 run one after another. Merging neighbouring CpGs into one window per query would cut this.
- **All CpGs (480,579 at 10x, more at 5x),** as Venkataraman et al. did: download one BAM at a time with its index, count locally, write a small table of counts per library, and delete the BAM. This takes about 3.6 to 10.9 hours of downloading and fits in the 31 GB free.

Either way:

- Assign strand of origin by FLAG pair: 99/147 for the top strand, 83/163 for the bottom. This is identical to XG here and is the rule BS-Snper uses.
- Count each fragment once by read name. Use scanBam and your own counting, not pileup, so the counts match the coverage files.
- Apply base quality 15, MAPQ 20 and a minimum depth of 5.
- Have the pilot agent check the coordinate convention of the merged CpG rows against the alignments first.
open_points: Whether the toggle should screen only the candidate DML or all tested CpGs (Venkataraman et al. screened all characterised CpGs and the candidate DML). This decides between remote queries and full downloads. It is a design choice for the author or the design lane.

Whether to pool all 22 libraries, as the merged BAM of Venkataraman did, or to call per library and take the union, and how triploid allele dosage enters the thresholds (minhetfreq 0.1, minhomfreq 0.85). The rule lane should settle this.

The Venkataraman notebook keeps only VCF rows whose REF is C and ALT is T (grep "C\tT"). It therefore drops the reverse-strand form (REF G, ALT A) of a variant at the G of a CpG. Whether the R rule should follow that literally or catch both forms is a fidelity question for the author.
Throughput from gannet varied between 2.0 and 21.5 MB/s, and remote queries between 1.3 and 10 s each. The estimates above rest on three range downloads and one 200-query run, on a single day.

I did not check whether running several fresh-handle query streams in parallel scales (the light-computing rule allowed one R process). The gannet server and the proxy (429 limits) would set the ceiling.

Files in the scratch folder that I did not write: code/t3_*.R, code/head_variants.sh, code/osf_dl.py, genome/, positions_200.csv, region_reads_zr3534_1.rds, bam_header_zr3534_1.rds, variant_file_probe.csv, downloads/bai/ and downloads/07-BS-SNPer.ipynb. They date from 00:33 to 00:44 UTC, before this run started, probably from an earlier attempt of this step. I did not use them. variant_file_probe.csv likewise finds no variant files (374 x 404; the only 6 x 200 are BAMs).
risks: A reused, explicitly opened remote BamFile silently returns no reads after its first query. A script written that way would find no variants and report no error.
About 2.5% of remote opens fail (5 of 200, 'Software caused connection abort'). Without retries some positions get NA or zero counts.

Rsamtools::pileup double counts the overlapping parts of mate pairs (85 to 89% of pairs overlap, by about 77 bp). Thresholds of depth and allele frequency would then differ from per-fragment counts and from the coverage files.
A full download of the 22 BAMs is 109 GB. While a 6.8 GB file is on disk, a second one prefetched (13.5 GB in all) still fits in the 31 GB free, but the hardening workflow also uses this disk.
The reference genome in the cache has no .fai. Building one must not write into the repository; the cache /home/user/gannet_cache is shared with the pipeline.

result.recommendation:
Keep config$modes as the loop variable, but derive it in run_config.R from six toggles that are all FALSE by default: optional = list(corrected, coverage_5x, overdispersion, exclude_ct_variants, go_gene_level, diagnostics), plus optional_min_coverage = 5. Leave min_coverage = 10 untouched.

The run's analyses are "legacy" (always, first) plus one analysis per reading (legacy, and corrected when that toggle is on). The 5x, MN-with-chi-squared and variant-exclusion toggles together set the suffix of those analyses: <reading>[_5x][_mn_chisq][_ctexcl].

run_pipeline.R gets the flags --corrected, --coverage-5x, --overdispersion, --exclude-ct-variants, --go-gene-level and --diagnostics. It passes them to every step in WGBS_OPTIONAL and gates the optional steps: 04b only with the exclusion, 10 only with gene-level GO, diagnostics after 13 only with --diagnostics, which also turns on corrected and gene-level GO.

Rules for the outputs:
- No toggle changes the bytes of a paper output.
- A table that today holds rows of several modes keeps its name for the legacy rows. Each optional analysis writes a `_<tag>` twin.
- Step 11's gene-level parts go to their own files, written only with gene-level GO on.
- Step 13 writes its corrected values to manuscript_values_corrected.csv, with "not run" when the analysis is off or its tables are absent.

Step 05:
- Each fit is cached in methylkit_<fit_tag>.rds, and the fingerprint gains a model part.
- The paper's calculateDiffMeth() call stays literally unchanged; overdispersion = "MN", test = "Chisq" is added only for MN analyses.
- The variant exclusion is applied after the fit, as Venkataraman et al. did, so it needs no new fit.
- The variant loci come from a lettered step, 01_pipeline/04b_ct_variant_loci.R.

Existing corrected and step-10 outputs keep their names. Run once with --corrected --go-gene-level, then the default run, and commit both. Check the result with tests T1 to T5 in design.md: expected bytes of the default run, the one-time refit, toggle invariance, reproduction of the committed corrected files, and a unit test over all 64 toggle combinations.

Venkataraman et al. also removed variant CpGs from the 5x CpG sets of their global description. Applying the exclusion in step 04 would need the variant step before 04 (number it 03b instead of 04b).
Variant step: a lettered step 04b (about 15 more lines in run_pipeline.R) or a helper called inside step 05. Renumbering would touch about 1,290 lines.

Step 13's legacy values read two committed diagnostic tables (fastq_read_names.csv, table1_group_means.csv; 15 expressions) that the default run does not regenerate. Should these move into a pipeline step?

Memory of a 5x step 05 is estimated only (6 to 8 GB import, 9 to 14 GB fits at 2 cores). A pilot with /usr/bin/time -v at WGBS_CORES=1 is needed, on a machine not shared with the hardening pass.
Step 10's two comparison tables (go_terms_by_analysis.csv, legacy_top10_at_gene_level.csv) cover only the analyses of the run that wrote them. Build them from all per-analysis files on disk instead?

result.summary:
I traced every place where the F test of methylKit's DML model (overdispersion "MN", test "F") is used, from the code through the outputs to the text. I wrote nothing to the repository. It is read only by the five F-test analyses of 06_diagnostics/dml_sensitivity.R: A1_ploidy_mn_f and A1_heat_mn_f (both modes), A2_interaction_mn_f (both modes), A4_ploidy_in_control_mn_f and A4_ploidy_in_heat_mn_f (legacy only). That is 8 of the 22 fits. Part 8 of library_methylation_level.R reads their lists. No step of 01_pipeline fits a model with the correction.

What comes from these fits:
- 8 DML list files.
- 8 rows of dml_counts.csv, and the F values of its column statistic_needed_for_a_single_call (84.1, 83.5, 89.5, 88.9, 250.6, 474.5).
- 5 rows of analyses.csv, with their reference_distribution text.
- 6 rows in each interaction_vs_shared_<mode>.csv.
- The analysis ids in the analyses column of permutation_reference.csv.
- 8 bars in figure_dml_sensitivity.
- All of corrected_dml_library_values.csv (145 legacy and 9 corrected CpGs) and corrected_dml_group_apart.csv (8 rows).
- 8 test_subset lists and 16 git-ignored cache files.
- 4 scratch p-values in the note column of manuscript_values_map.csv. They carry into 05_manuscript/manuscript_values.csv.

The main result is that every chi-squared counterpart can be computed from the cache without refitting. methylKit:::logReg uses the same statistic, D/phi, for both tests. Each F fit has a cached fit without the correction on the same design. From the two, I derived the chi-squared p-values for all 8 F fits in about 5 minutes, at under 3 GB of virtual memory. For the two pairs that also have a cached chi-squared fit, the derivation gives the same DML lists exactly (14 and 185), with p within 2e-8 relative and q within 2e-14.

Chi-squared numbers, legacy mode with corrected mode in parentheses:
- Ploidy: 14 DML (14). 168 CpGs significant.
- Heat: 185 DML (157). 1,124 CpGs significant.
- Interaction: 242 DML (231). None of them among the 200 (159) overlap loci.
- Ploidy among the controls: 10 DML, 3 of them among the draft's 1,038.
- Ploidy among the heat-treated: 1,093 DML, 179 of them among the 1,038.
- Share of eligible CpGs with p below 0.05: 7.3%, 13.2%, 23.3%, 10.4%, 24.6% (same order).

I found 67 statements that rest on the F fits; 30 of them name the test. They are in issues.md (I-01, I-02, I-06 items 2 to 7 with its rating, What follows and Options, I-07, I-08, I-49 item 7, the corrections table), README.md, 06_diagnostics/README.md, the plan, the handoff, the values map, and the two scripts.

Several readings of the audit log change in substance with the chi-squared fit:
1. The lists are 14 and 185, not 2 and 16.
2. The heat list holds up under the coverage filter (157 of 185 kept). The text says it is "not stable at its threshold".
3. The ploidy pair is no longer at the edge: q is 1.2e-8 where the text gives 0.0099. Both CpGs of the pair are also called inside the heat cohort, where the text says neither is.
4. CpGs whose dispersion estimate is not above 1 are a minority of the chi-squared lists, not "most":
   - ploidy: 1 of 14
   - heat: 2 of 185
   - interaction: 5 of 242
   - controls: 2 of 10
   - heat cohort: 172 of 1,093
5. Looser q thresholds give 37 ploidy CpGs at q < 0.05 and 52 at q < 0.1. The text says "a looser threshold gives no list".
6. The corrected interaction becomes a list of 242 CpGs, not 2.

The argument that the corrected test is not calibrated can then rest only on the relabelling shares, which are already computed (7.19%, 2.16% and 0.47% below 0.05, 0.01 and 0.001).

Computing needed:
- 6 new methylKit fits:
  - A1_ploidy_mn_chisq and A1_heat_mn_chisq in corrected mode
  - A2_interaction_mn_chisq in both modes
  - A4_ploidy_in_control_mn_chisq and A4_ploidy_in_heat_mn_chisq in legacy mode

result.recommendation:
Build design D2. The default run produces the paper only. Any switch makes an optional run that writes only under not_adopted/.

**Settings in run_config.R.** Remove config$modes and add config$optional with these defaults:
- coverage_filter_of_methods = FALSE (a), token corrected
- coverage_standard = 10L (b), set to 5L for token cov5
- overdispersion_chisq = FALSE (c), token mnchisq; MN with Chisq only
- exclude_ct_variants = FALSE (d), token ctexcl
- gene_level_go = FALSE (e)
- diagnostics = character(0) (f)

run_config.R resolves these into one config$analysis. Freeze the paper's settings (min_coverage 10, import_min_coverage 2, q 0.01, difference 20, percentile 99.9): editing any of them stops every step.

**Switches of run_pipeline.R:** --coverage-filter, --coverage 5|10, --overdispersion, --exclude-ct-variants, --gene-level-go, --diagnostics [all|names], --plan. They reach the steps as WGBS_* environment variables.

**Outputs.**
- The paper keeps 04_output/<step>/ and 05_manuscript/ with present names. Spanning tables hold the paper's rows only.
- Each optional analysis gets 04_output/not_adopted/<id>/<step>/, with _legacy replaced by _<id> in file names, and an analysis.csv stamp.
- not_adopted/comparisons/ rebuilds the spanning tables from every analysis folder present, paper first. With legacy and corrected present they equal today's tables byte for byte.
- Step 10 moves wholly to not_adopted/legacy/, not_adopted/corrected/ and comparisons/.

**Steps.** Steps 04-09 run once for the analysis of the run, and step 09 also runs for optional analyses. Step 10 runs only with (e). Steps 11 and 12 run in paper runs only; the step 10 dependent part of step 11 moves out of the paper.

**Step 05 cache.** One cache file per fit id, methylkit_<fit_id>.rds, where the fit id is the analysis id without ctexcl. The fingerprint gains the model. The variant exclusion is applied after the test, so it never refits.

**Step 13.** A paper part writes the paper tables without corrected columns. An optional part evaluates a templated expression_optional (A = analysis id; tab() reads the analysis folder, paper_tab() reads the paper) for every analysis folder present. Rows whose input files are absent read "not run".

**Variant step.** The new R step is 01_pipeline/optional/ct_variant_loci.R, unnumbered. It writes not_adopted/ct_variants/tables/ct_variant_cpgs.csv.gz, committed once.

**Order of work.**
1. Move the existing files with git mv in a separate commit.
2. Build the change.
3. Run the 13 tests of section 12. The core ones: paper folders unchanged by every optional run (checksums); paper spanning tables equal the committed legacy rows (code/compare_paper_rows.py); the corrected run reproduces the moved files; --overdispersion gives 14 and 185 DML matching the sensitivity lists; the templated expressions with A = corrected reproduce the 263 present corrected values.
4. Measure 5x memory at WGBS_CORES=1 before any full 5x run.
open_points: Byte identity cannot hold for 10 paper files: the 8 spanning tables, manuscript_values.csv and manuscript_values_summary.csv. Today they include corrected-mode rows or columns, and the paper-only default must drop them. The paper rows stay byte-identical, which the comparer checks. The alternative is to keep the mixed tables in the paper folders; that keeps the bytes but puts optional rows among the paper's outputs. The author should choose.

Step 11, a paper step, reads step 10, which is optional. Proposed: move its gene-level parts out of the paper. This changes named_terms_results_3_4.csv (5 columns) and semantic_summary.csv (1 row). The alternative is that the paper keeps reading the committed step 10 tables.

15 paper values rest on two diagnostic tables (fastq_read_names.csv, table1_group_means.csv) that the default run does not regenerate. One option is to promote table1_group_means.R into the paper steps.
Each optional run makes one analysis (the switches compose). A list of analyses per run could be added later.
Should step 09 (the paper's GO procedure) run for optional analyses? Proposed yes, following handoff item 3. Steps 08 and 09 have never been run on DML sets as small as 14.
Freezing the paper thresholds stops threshold exploration. If the author wants that, it would be another toggle.
The memory of step 05 at 5x is unmeasured. It may exceed what the machine can give while the other 10 GB workflow runs.
If the variant design adds sub-settings (PASS records only; check the G of each CpG), each needs its own id token so that two different variant lists never share a folder.
This design does not cover the variant step itself (rule, run time, disk). That belongs to the variant scoping agents.
risks: Changing fit_mode() invalidates the cached paper fit, so the first run refits for about 18 minutes at 2 cores. The output must then be compared byte for byte (diffmeth and united gz files on the same OS).

If a step reads config$min_coverage where it should read the analysis's coverage, an optional run gives wrong optional results. The reverse mistake, where the paper reads the analysis value, is prevented: the paper settings are frozen and optional runs never write paper folders.

The scripted rewrite of 263 expressions could alter a paper expression. Test: md5 of the expression_legacy column before and after, and equality of the templated values with today's regenerated_corrected values.
About 70 sites in 11 diagnostics scripts must point at not_adopted/corrected/. A missed site fails loudly with a missing file, not silently.

The 5x step 05 may run out of memory at 2 cores. The 5x united and diffmeth tables (about 107 MB and 71 MB) exceed the 50 MB commit rule and GitHub's 100 MB limit, so they must be git-ignored. A clone must then refit to get them.
The hardening pass is still editing files: step 11 changed at 01:38. Line numbers and counts in design.md may shift before the toggles pass starts.

I wrote the plan to plan.md in my scratch directory. It removes the F test of methylKit's DML model and keeps the correction with the chi-squared test only (overdispersion "MN", test "Chisq"). Nothing in the repository was changed.

**Cross-check of the two inventories**
- The dependency trace's 06_diagnostics/README.md line numbers (S40-S50) are all off by 35. Two of them, lines 48 and 49, are the ELISA and %mCpG two-way ANOVA rows ("interaction F"), so an edit made at those numbers would hit an F statistic of the draft. S09 (issues.md) belongs at 299-300 and S67 (library_methylation_level.R part 8) at 54-62.
- 40 explicit or unnamed hits of the term sweep were missing from the trace. Each is now covered or explained in statements_checked.csv, which has 83 rows (67 from the trace plus 16 added).
- Neither inventory has three values-map rows that also rest on the A2 F fit: R3.5-049, D4.9-002 and D3.5x-001. The sweep missed issues.md 170 and classed plan line 100 and the values-map interaction notes as unrelated.
- I opened the files and confirmed well over 40 lines across issues.md, the READMEs, the plan, the handoff, the values map and both scripts. The relevant files have not changed since commit 435f971 (current HEAD is 671feca).

**Code changes**
- In 06_diagnostics/dml_sensitivity.R, each of the 5 F analyses is replaced by its chi-squared twin. This keeps 22 fits: 16 in legacy mode and 6 in corrected mode.
- The F branches go: test validation (line 425), figure label (452), reference_distribution (457-459) and the qf statistic (997-999). Header lines 13-17, 31-32, 100-105, 107-122 and 176-179 are reworded.
- The cache signature does not include `modes`, so the two existing chi-squared legacy fits stay valid. Only 6 fits are new.
- library_methylation_level.R lines 54-57, 73, 247 and 415 are pointed at the `_mn_chisq` lists. No other script reads the F outputs.

**Fits**
- The 6 new fits take about 56 minutes at WGBS_CORES=3, plus about 10 minutes for the tables. library_methylation_level.R then takes about 2 minutes, and step 13 is rerun after the values-map edits.
- The cache is reused only if the md5 of the two united_cpg tables is unchanged after the hardening rerun (now 8e7f5d67... and ebec40d3...). Otherwise all 22 fits are redone, about 3 hours.

- The F against chi-squared tail comparison and "not a middle course".
- "The corrected test holds its level on average".
- "Most corrected calls are uncorrected".
